solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Fellow American in the summer gala (8)

blocks.note: estival is the American spelling of aestival, 'of the summer'

annotation.surface: An American visitor turns up at a summer gala.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'American' a person; it is really a spelling label, marking ESTIVAL as the US form of the British aestival.
annotation.definitionFit: A festival is a gala: a public celebration with entertainment.

entries.clue: Notes losing volume without loud musicians (6)

indicatorNotes.losing: the notes lose their V, so it is taken out
indicatorNotes.without: 'without' in its old sense of outside: FI…ERS goes outside F

blocks.note: V = volume, removed to leave FIERS
f = forte, loud in music, placed inside FI…ERS

annotation.surface: A band's notes go quiet while the loud players keep going.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Notes' looks musical beside 'loud' and 'musicians', but these are banknotes: a fiver is a British five-pound note.
annotation.definitionFit: Fifers are musicians who play the fife, a small flute.

entries.clue: Hurt protecting first in royal succession (6)

indicatorNotes.protecting: STING wraps around the letter it protects

blocks.note: first letter of royal, placed inside ST…ING

annotation.surface: Someone is hurt shielding the heir in a royal line of succession.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Royal succession' reads as one phrase about thrones; the break falls between them, and 'succession' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a run of events one after another, like a series of victories, is a succession.

entries.clue: Locomotive, once smooth, sounded rough (4,5)

indicatorNotes.sounded: HORSE is said the same as hoarse

blocks.note: to iron is to smooth out creases

annotation.surface: An old steam engine that once ran smoothly now wheezes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks the definition as dated: iron horse was a nineteenth-century name for a steam locomotive.
annotation.definitionFit: Iron horse was an old popular name for a railway locomotive.

entries.clue: Pasta menu — it’s hopeless for wine (4,8)

indicatorNotes.hopeless: the letters are a hopeless mess, so rearrange them

annotation.surface: A diner complains that the pasta menu is useless for choosing a wine.
annotation.walkthrough: The Italian surface suits the Italian answer: the letters of 'pasta menu it's' make the sparkling wine from Asti.
annotation.definitionFit: Asti spumante is a sweet sparkling white wine from Piedmont.

entries.clue: Energy in powerful creature’s legs (6)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' in its plain positional sense: E sits inside the stag's, between STAG and its possessive S

blocks.note: a stag's, the possessive supplying the S

annotation.surface: A stag's strong legs are full of energy.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'legs' a stag's limbs; here they are legs of a journey or race.
annotation.definitionFit: Stages are legs of a journey, tour or relay.

entries.clue: Crowd removing last of their underwear (5)

indicatorNotes.removing: to remove is to take away, so the crowd word loses a letter
indicatorNotes.last of: that letter is the final one of 'their'

blocks.note: last letter of their, taken out

annotation.surface: A crowd of people strip off their underwear.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a group undressing; 'removing' actually works on a single letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a thong is one kind of underwear, a narrow strip of cloth.

entries.clue: Good hypothesis abandoned by fool’s initiative (8)

indicatorNotes.abandoned by: the fool leaves the hypothesis, so ASS comes out

blocks.note: an ass is a fool, taken out to leave UMPTION

annotation.surface: A fool drops a good theory, showing little initiative.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': the wordplay is initiative. 'Fool's initiative' looks like one possessive phrase, but the definition is 'initiative' alone.
annotation.definitionFit: Gumption is initiative: resourceful common sense.

entries.clue: Paper towels and other stuff (8)

blocks.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
towels as a verb: dries with a towel

annotation.surface: A shopping list: paper towels and other household bits.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Paper towels' is one household item in the surface; split them, 'towels' becomes a verb, and 'paper' is The Sun, a British daily tabloid.
annotation.definitionFit: Sundries are miscellaneous items, other stuff not worth listing.

entries.clue: Really old river banks no doubt (8)

indicatorNotes.banks: to bank something is to line its sides, as a river's banks do, so FORTH goes around the rest

annotation.surface: Someone declares that a certain river's banks are very ancient.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Really old' looks like the definition, since forsooth is an archaic word; it is wordplay, and 'no doubt' at the end is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An archaic adverb: forsooth meant 'in truth', which is what 'no doubt' asserts.

entries.clue: Awfully old tomb of awfully old people (6)

blocks.note: the second 'old', scrambled by the 'awfully' before it

annotation.surface: A very ancient burial place for very ancient people.
annotation.walkthrough: The repeated 'awfully old' plays two roles: first it means 'extremely ancient' in the definition, then 'awfully' scrambles OLD in the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a dolmen is a prehistoric burial chamber of standing stones capped by a slab.

entries.clue: Winning phase in pontoon (7,5)

blocks.note: landing a contract or a prize is winning it

annotation.surface: The point in a hand of pontoon where you know you have won.
annotation.walkthrough: Pontoon is a British name for the card game twenty-one, which makes 'winning phase' look like part of the game; here it is a floating jetty.
annotation.definitionFit: A pontoon is a floating platform, the kind used as a landing stage for boats.

entries.clue: Farm managed by Cornish extremists (5)

indicatorNotes.extremists: the extremes of 'Cornish' are its first and last letters

blocks.note: to run a business is to manage it
first and last letters of Cornish

annotation.surface: A farm in Cornwall run by radicals.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cornish extremists' suggests Cornish nationalists; it only asks for the outside letters of 'Cornish'.
annotation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large farm, especially for cattle.

entries.clue: Butcher, the source of some amusement (9)

indicatorNotes.the source of: the source of a word is where it starts: its first letter

annotation.surface: A butcher who is a figure of fun.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Butcher' is a verb here, and slaughter can be a verb too, so the swap holds.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both verbs: to kill animals for meat, or people savagely and in numbers.

entries.clue: Tennis shot pulverized by sudden attack (6,6)

blocks.note: a stroke is a sudden seizure

annotation.surface: A tennis shot smashed by an opponent's sudden assault.
annotation.walkthrough: 'By' just places GROUND beside STROKE; the tennis surface makes 'sudden attack' look like an aggressive shot, but it is medical.
annotation.definitionFit: A ground stroke is a tennis shot played after the ball has bounced.

entries.clue: Den put up here to use playfully (9)

indicatorNotes.playfully: the letters are played with, so rearranged

annotation.surface: A children's den set up here for playing in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put up' means raised high, which is what makes a den a treehouse; 'playfully' suits a children's hideout.
annotation.definitionFit: A treehouse is a den built up among the branches of a tree.

entries.clue: Writer said to tick all the boxes (5,3)

annotation.surface: An author praised for doing everything expected of him.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tick all the boxes' sounds like the idiom for meeting every requirement; read literally, it is ticking items on a list.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom read literally: marking each item on a list as done, box by box.

entries.clue: Broil hake, chopped nuts and brassica (8)

indicatorNotes.chopped: hake has its end chopped off
indicatorNotes.nuts: crazy, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A recipe: grilled hake with chopped nuts and a cabbage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chopped nuts' reads as a garnish; 'chopped' trims HAKE and 'nuts' scrambles the lot.
annotation.definitionFit: Kohlrabi is a brassica, a cabbage with a swollen edible stem.

entries.clue: Folk concerts jeered, mostly by nurses (12)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most of the word, so its last letter goes

annotation.surface: Folk concerts booed, largely by nursing staff.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface has the nurses doing the jeering; 'by' only means 'beside', joining the two parts.
annotation.definitionFit: A hootenanny is an informal gathering with folk music.

entries.clue: Battle to take away the last sausage (6)

blocks.note: the sea battle of 480 BC in which the Greeks beat the Persians, named after an island

annotation.surface: A struggle to grab the last sausage on the plate.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a fight over food; the battle is a proper name, Salamis.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: salami is one kind of sausage, cured and spiced.

entries.clue: Capital letters in order to end stanzas (6)

blocks.note: the first of the two letters ending stanzAS
'in order' = next, afterwards; it goes between the two letters

annotation.surface: Instructions on which capital letters close each verse.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Capital letters' reads as upper case; 'Capital' alone is the definition. Stanzas ends in A and S, and the wordplay names those two letters in order.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Athens is one capital city, that of Greece.

entries.clue: Nuns say church table is wonky (9)

indicatorNotes.wonky: askew, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Nuns remark that the church table wobbles.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Say' reads as the nuns speaking; it marks them as an example of celibates.
annotation.definitionFit: Nuns are one kind of celibate, having taken vows of chastity.

entries.clue: Taking a risk leaving school to make jewellery (5)

blocks.note: a gam is a school of whales, removed

annotation.surface: Someone drops out of school, gambling on a career in jewellery.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leaving school' reads as a teenager quitting education; the school is a gam, a pod of whales.
annotation.definitionFit: A slang term from hip-hop culture for flashy, showy jewellery.

entries.clue: Courage shown by the artillery (5)

indicatorNotes.shown by: the answer is on show inside the words that follow

annotation.surface: The gunners displayed bravery.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a report of gunners' bravery; the answer sits in plain view across the break between two words.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: the heart is traditionally the seat of courage, as in 'take heart' or 'lose heart'.

entries.clue: Agree to a drink around wild animals (6)

blocks.note: to OK something is to agree to it
a sip is a small drink

annotation.surface: Someone agrees to have a drink among the wild animals on safari.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Around' reads as 'among' in the surface; it turns SIP back to front.
annotation.definitionFit: Okapis are shy African forest animals related to the giraffe.

entries.clue: Treat us badly crossing a swamp (8)

indicatorNotes.badly: treated badly, so the letters are jumbled
indicatorNotes.crossing: the jumbled letters go across A, around it

annotation.surface: A complaint about being mistreated while wading across a swamp.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swamp' is a noun in the surface but a verb as the definition: to swamp is to drench.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both verbs: flooding something until it can hold no more water.

entries.clue: Edge of hoop coated with iron (6)

indicatorNotes.coated with: the hoop is coated with iron on both sides

blocks.note: Fe, the chemical symbol for iron, wrapped around RING

annotation.surface: The rim of a hoop has an iron coating.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Edge of hoop' reads as one phrase; 'Edge' alone is the definition and 'of' links it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the outer margin of an area, as in the outskirts of a town.

entries.clue: Northern meat retains its advantages (8)

indicatorNotes.retains: the meat holds the N inside it

annotation.surface: Northern meat keeps its good qualities.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Its' looks like a pronoun for the meat; it simply supplies the last three letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the good things something brings, the points in its favour.
